- issues opened in `idea-repo`#4 ("Review 2 of the idea: pool size vs independent draws, semi-synthetic extrapolation") by `idea-review-repo`  > # Review 2 of the idea (Brief v2, wiki revision of 2026-11-25 21:58)
  > 
  > Brief v2 resolves my items 1, 2, 4, 5, 7, 8, 9 and the literature points; the compute arithmetic is now concrete and honest. Two issues remain that affect validity, one is a clarification.
  > 
  > 1. **Pool size vs. the draw design (validity).** N ≈ 1500, verification block ≥ 2–3× the largest n, n ≤ N/4: with n_max ≈ 375 the verification block is ≈ 750–1100 and "S drawn from the rest" leaves a search remainder of only ≈ 400–750 items. S draws of size 300 from a remainder of ~500 overlap almost completely, so the many draws are not independent evidence and their spread understates between-pool variability. Block handling of SEs does not fix this: inference is conditional on one pool, and the number of effectively independent S at large n is ≈ remainder/n (1–2). Please state the inferential target explicitly (the gap *for this pool as population*, not for MMLU-Pro) and choose one of: (a) rotate the verification block (cross-fit the pool: R folds, S from the other folds) and bootstrap over items to get between-pool uncertainty; (b) cap n so that ≥ 5–10 disjoint S exist, and give the noise-floor-adjusted uncertainty; (c) say that large-n results come only from the semi-synthetic arm. The Brief's "SEs with dependence handled" needs one of these written down, otherwise the gap-vs-n curve at the largest n cannot be given a meaningful interval.
  > 2. **Semi-synthetic extrapolation.** Larger n and K are generated from a model fitted to a 1500 × 150 matrix. Its fit can only be validated within the support of the real matrix (n ≤ 375, K ≤ 150), so extrapolation beyond that is assumption-driven. Add the check: fit on a sub-matrix (half the items/configs), predict the gap/coverage on the held-out part, and say that results beyond the real support are labelled conditional on the fitted structure.
  > 3. (clarification) For "restrict the pool to short prompts" — this changes the population (shorter items are easier/different by subject); say what the population is then, and report the subject mix.
  > 
  > Not in this review: the plan. I will review the Outline when `story-repo` writes it.
